title: The 2003 Blackout's Cause Was Growing Outside #shorts
summary: The 14 Aug 2003 blackout was the worst in North American history. The US-Canada task force listed inadequate tree trimming among its causes.
sources: August 14, 2003, saw the worst blackout in North American history; the causes the US-Canada task force named include inadequate situational awareness and inadequate tree trimming (US DOE, Blackout 2003: task force final report, 5 Apr 2004): https://www.energy.gov/oe/articles/blackout-2003-us-canada-task-force-presents-final-report-onblackout-august-2003

Supply must match demand for the grid to stay stable; transformers step voltage up and down between the power plant, long-distance lines and distribution lines; the Eastern and Western interconnections are linked to Canada's grid (EIA, Electricity explained: delivery to consumers): https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/electricity/delivery-to-consumers.php

scenes.narration: North America's worst blackout had a very ordinary cause.
August {14|fourteenth}, {2003|two thousand three}. The worst blackout in North American history.
A task force studied what went wrong. Its list of causes included blind spots in the control rooms.
Trees. That's the ordinary cause behind the worst blackout in North America.
